profilePeriod: Public record through 2026-10-02, prioritising 2026 policies; older evidence explicitly dated.
scopeNote: Answers to hypotheticals are source-constrained simulations, not a claim Burnham completed this quiz. Dedicated searches covered all twelve axes; individual unaddressed proposals require cautious inference, not invented quotations.

sources.evidence: Current office confirmed by official biography.

sources.evidence: Public control of utilities, council housing, national care, regional power, electoral reform, domestic procurement, nuclear and renewables, AI governance, fiscal rules, NATO and Ukraine.

sources.evidence: Burnham secured regional transport, housing, skills responsibilities and a single block grant.

sources.title: Mayors share of income tax
sources.evidence: Regional revenue retention and devolved powers, keeping strategic national responsibilities.

sources.title: UK-France cooperation
sources.evidence: Burnham supports border control through European cooperation and action against smuggling gangs; protects vulnerable migrants.

sources.title: Sentencing restrictions
sources.evidence: Excludes serious offences from earlier release, supports tagging and victim exclusion zones, while ending indefinite IPP imprisonment.

sources.title: Public Office Accountability Bill evidence
sources.evidence: Burnham gives evidence supporting public accountability and parity of legal representation for victims.

sources.title: First overseas visit to Ukraine
sources.evidence: Supports Ukrainian defence and releasing component information for missile assembly with France.

sources.title: ITV interview on Europe
sources.evidence: Advocates closer EU relations for growth but has not committed to immediate rejoining; cautions about divisive referendums.

sources.title: First-person interview with Burnham
sources.evidence: Values Catholic community and stable families but is uncertain about God. Supports same-sex marriage and abortion compassion; defended his Iraq vote. Historical testimony, not proof of unchanged current policy.

sources.title: Catholic identity and contemporary politics
sources.evidence: Reports Catholic social teaching as political influence alongside dissent on marriage and abortion; corroborates historical interview.

sources.title: Greater Manchester carbon-neutral progress
sources.evidence: 2038 carbon-neutral ambition, investment-led clean air policy, renewable power for electric buses and green economic growth.

sources.title: Scottish Government portrait on Commons
sources.evidence: Scottish Government photograph, CC BY 2.0; cropped on Commons, resized and compressed to 480x640 locally, visually checked.

sources.title: PA interview on care before assisted dying
sources.evidence: Support for assisted dying in principle is conditional on safeguards and adequately funded palliative and social care; he wants care reform first.

sources.title: LBC report on single-sex guidance
sources.evidence: Supports trans rights while accepting implementation of Supreme Court single-sex guidance fairly and compassionately, avoiding marginalisation.

sources.title: BBC Scotland interview on drug decriminalisation
sources.evidence: Opposes personal-use drug decriminalisation, citing the message about harm to young people.
sources.verificationNote: Direct BBC page inaccessible to the web tool; attributed BBC-origin search result and rendered mirror exposed the interview text. Treat this narrower evidence boundary explicitly.

estrutura.interpretation: Regional fiscal and service autonomy, not secession or abolition of national standards.

representacao.interpretation: Electoral reform and cross-party collaboration; direct referendums approached cautiously, not unqualified direct democracy.

poder.interpretation: Protect victims with strong criminal enforcement, yet police/state accountability and due process. Neither police-state nor anarchist. September 2026 BBC interview rejects personal-use drug decriminalisation (search/mirror evidence boundary noted).

imigracao.interpretation: Enforce managed borders against illegal crossings while working with partners and protecting migrants; neither open borders nor ethnic exclusion.

diplomacia.interpretation: NATO and material military support for Ukraine; two-state diplomacy. Not absolute pacifism or glorification of war.

intervencao.interpretation: International security cooperation and active Ukraine support; earlier Iraq vote prevents blanket non-interventionist attribution.

economia.interpretation: Essential utilities and care under public control, council housing, while supporting private enterprise outside essentials. Not abolition of capitalism.

controle.interpretation: Sector planning and regulation with fiscal discipline, regional coordination and private business growth; not total central planning.

comercio.interpretation: Closer European trade and investment alongside domestic procurement and reindustrialisation. Not autarky or unrestricted trade in every sector.

religiao.interpretation: Catholic social teaching and community matter publicly; theological uncertainty and dissent on church rules prevent theocratic attribution.

moral.interpretation: Equal marriage and abortion rights coexist with preference for stable caring families; not all culturally radical policies follow. Recent support for trans rights includes compliance with single-sex law; assisted dying support is conditional on properly funded care and safeguards.

tecnologia.interpretation: AI innovation with risk governance, clean energy including nuclear, green urban transport; neither anti-technology ruralism nor unqualified transhumanism.

probableNeighbours.jeremy-corbyn: Burnham combines support for NATO and armed Ukraine with public services, stronger border enforcement, fiscal rules and regional devolution; do not copy Corbyn.
probableNeighbours.tony-blair: Burnham advocates public control of essential utilities and electoral reform, with deeper regional fiscal autonomy; do not copy Blair.
